specification.problem: Approximate MaxCut on small unweighted regular graphs G=(V,E), n=|V|, m=|E|, using p-layer QAOA with parameters (gamma,beta) and Z-basis readout.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Build the p-layer QAOA circuit (p=1..3) on n qubits for a tiny explicit instance (for example the 3-regular K4 graph or a 2-regular ring), with no ancillas. Compute <C> from the statevector or counts, and take the best sampled cut. Out of scope: the proof of the 0.6924 bound, the closed-form p=1 edge expectation for 3-regular graphs, the large-p strategy, and the explicit classical preprocessing based on local subgraphs for large graphs.

symbols.meaning: unweighted graph, vertex i maps to qubit i
phase-separator and mixer angles of layer l
MaxCut objective operator, diagonal in the Z basis
mixer Hamiltonian, the sum of X_i
bitstring, with z_i the bit of vertex i

equations.label: MaxCut objective
equations.description: C counts the cut edges. Each term acts on 2 qubits.
equations.justification: Standard MaxCut Hamiltonian. The abstract only says the gate locality is at most that of the objective.

equations.label: QAOA state
equations.description: Start from |+>^n. Layer l applies the phase separator and then the mixer, with layer 1 applied first.
equations.justification: Standard QAOA ansatz, consistent with the abstract's integer p and its circuit of local unitaries.

equations.label: Gate decomposition
equations.latex: e^{-i\gamma(1-Z_iZ_j)/2}\simeq \mathrm{RZZ}(\gamma)_{ij}=CX_{ij}\,RZ_j(\gamma)\,CX_{ij}\ (\text{up to global phase});\quad e^{-i\beta X_i}=RX_i(2\beta)
equations.description: Qiskit gates for each edge term and each mixer term. RZZ(theta)=exp(-i theta ZZ/2), so the e^{-i gamma C} edge term gives RZZ(-gamma) up to a global phase. The sign of the angle depends on the convention, so the angle sign must be checked in the builder.
equations.justification: The gate count is O(p*m), which matches the abstract's claim that depth is linear in p times the number of constraints.
assumptions: The sign convention is fixed so that maximizing <C> gives the largest cut

equations.label: Expected cut and readout
equations.description: Estimate <C> from the statevector or from counts, or keep the best sampled cut. In a Qiskit counts key, vertex i is bits[::-1][i].
equations.abstract_quote: The algorithm depends on an integer $p\geq 1$ and the quality of the approximation improves as $p$ is increased.
equations.justification: The abstract implies an approximation quality measured by the objective. The estimator itself is the standard one.

equations.label: 2-regular ring ratio
equations.description: Known result for rings of large girth, recalled from background. It is not stated in the abstract and can serve as a sanity check for a large ring.
equations.justification: Recalled from the QAOA literature, not verified. It holds for rings with n>2p+1.

registers.name: q
registers.role: one qubit per vertex, no ancillas

specification.initial_state: |0>^n, then H on every qubit, giving |+>^n

steps.description: For l=1..p, apply RZZ-type phase gates on every edge using gamma_l.
For l=1..p, apply RX(2*beta_l) on every qubit after the phase layer.
Read the statevector or measure all qubits. Compute <C> or the best sampled cut. The angles come from a classical grid search or optimization on F_p.

specification.measurement: Measure all n qubits in the Z basis only if counts are required. Otherwise read the statevector without measurements. Qiskit little-endian order applies, so vertex i is bits[::-1][i].
specification.classical_postprocessing: Evaluate the cut of each sampled bitstring and keep the maximum, or compute F_p. Optimize (gamma, beta) by a classical grid search, using the full small-graph simulation as a stand-in for the local-subgraph evaluation.
assumptions: The instance is a tiny unweighted regular graph, chosen by the builder.
The angle sign and RZZ convention are fixed by the builder so that maximizing <C> gives the largest cut.
n is within the qubit cap.
missing_information: The explicit p=1 closed-form edge expectation for 3-regular graphs is not given.
The optimal angles are not given.
The large-p strategy is not specified.
The detailed classical preprocessing method is not specified.
